title: Development of a vector control training package for wash and health practitioners in the africa region.
description:
(Find the complete folder with all relevant information including the RFP here ) Terms of Reference Title of Assignment Development of a Vector Control Training Package for WASH and Health Practitioners in the Africa Region Project Name WASH Surge Localization Programme Project Country Global (pilot training to be conducted in Ethiopia or South Sudan) 1. Introduction The Netherlands Red Cross (NLRC) and partners are working to strengthen local capacities for emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and response across Africa. In line with their auxiliary role to the public authorities, and within the framework of localization, National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies frequently act as first responders during disease outbreaks, flooding, displacement crises, and other emergencies. Vector-borne diseases continue to pose a significant public health burden in many countries where the Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies operate. At the same time, vector control knowledge among WASH and Health practitioners varies considerably. There is a need for accessible, practical training materials that can be used by National Societies, surge personnel, and humanitarian practitioners to improve knowledge and decision-making related to vector control. The NLRC therefore seeks a consultant to develop a comprehensive training package on vector control that can be delivered by facilitators with a fair understanding of the subject matter. The package will be piloted during a training event planned for December 2026 in either Ethiopia or South Sudan. 2. Background and Context Vector-borne diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in many humanitarian settings. Climate change, population movements, urbanization, environmental degradation, and weak health systems are contributing to changes in disease transmission patterns and increasing the risk of outbreaks. Humanitarian organizations are increasingly expected to integrate vector control considerations into emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programmes. While specialist expertise is sometimes available, many WASH and Health practitioners involved in programme design and implementation have limited formal training in vector control. The Red Cross movement has an important role to play through: Community engagement , risk communication and behaviour change Environmental management Vector surveillance and risk assessment Support to outbreak preparedness and response including community-based surveillance Coordination with health and WASH actors Integration of vector control into humanitarian programming To strengthen these capacities, a practical training package is required that can be delivered in different country contexts and adapted to local disease priorities. 3. Purpose, Objectives and Deliverables Purpose To develop a practical, participatory and easy-to-facilitate vector control training package for WASH and Health practitioners working in humanitarian and development settings. Overall Objective To increase the knowledge and understanding of vector-borne disease prevention and vector control among WASH and Health practitioners, enabling them to support the design, implementation and monitoring of appropriate vector control interventions. Specific Objectives The training package should enable participants to: Understand the epidemiology and transmission pathways of major vector-borne diseases. Understand the roles and responsibilities of WASH, Health and community actors in vector control. Conduct basic vector-related risk assessments. Select appropriate vector control interventions based on context and risk. Understand operational, environmental and safety considerations. Integrate vector control into preparedness, anticipatory action and humanitarian emergency responses. Coordinate with relevant health, WASH and government stakeholders. Scope of the Training Package The consultant should develop a 3 days training package with different modules and exercises, allowing for a one to three days training depending on the modules used. The training should cover, at minimum: Vector-borne Diseases Introduction to: Malaria (with description of different malaria carrying subspecies) Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever, Schistosomiasis, Trypanosomiasis and other relevant diseases common in African humanitarian settings Vector Control Approaches Introduction to Environmental mechanical biological and chemical and integrated Vector Management (IVM). Humanitarian Context The context considered for the training include, vector control during emergencies**,** vector control during displacement and camp settings, Flood-related vector risks, Urban vector control challenges as well as for the Red Cross important Community-based approaches, and Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI) Planning and Decision Making The training should include a section focusing on health and surveillance data, risk assessment, Intervention selection, Monitoring and evaluation, Coordination mechanisms Safety and Environmental Considerations This should include Safe handling of equipment and chemicals Environmental risks Waste management Safeguarding and community acceptance Emerging and other relevant Topics Climate change and vector-borne diseases Insecticide resistance, new and emerging vector control tools such as spatial repellents, Operational challenges in humanitarian settings Deliverables The consultant will with the support of the NLRC and UNICEF will be expected to provide: Review and compilation of existing vector control training materials from organizations such as: IFRC, WHO, UNICEF and NGO’s working on vector control and identify materials that can be adapted and referenced. The consultant will develop a complete facilitator package in English including: Facilitator guide, Agenda for a 3-day version, Session plans, Facilitation notes, Interactive exercises Possible case studies and group work exercises, Quizzes and knowledge checks Participant package that should include: Participant manual, Handouts, Reference materials, Reading list Links to online resources PowerPoint presentation deck(s) suitable for use by non-specialist facilitators. Training evaluation package including: Pre-training assessment Post-training assessment Participant evaluation forms Facilitation of a pilot training in December 2026 in Ethiopia South Sudan or other country in the region and incorporation of lessons learned into the final training package(optional). 4. Profile of the Desired Consultant The consultant should possess: Minimum 7 years of professional experience in vector control, public health, entomology, or related fields. Demonstrated experience in humanitarian settings. Experience with vector control in Africa, preferably in both emergency and development contexts. Proven experience in developing training curricula and adult learning materials. Strong facilitation skills. Experience working with Red Cross/Red Crescent, UN agencies, government institutions or international NGOs is an advantage. Excellent written and spoken English. Experience integrating participatory adult learning methodologies. 5. Methodology The consultant is expected to: Conduct a brief desk review of existing training resources. Consult with NLRC, IFRC, UNICEF and selected technical experts. Develop draft training materials. Revise materials based on feedback. Facilitate the pilot training. Produce a final training package reflecting lessons learned from the pilot. 6. Planning Indicative timeline: Activity Timeline Contracting consultant - Week of 9th November 2026 Desk review and consultations - November 20th 2026 Draft training package - November 25th 2026 Review and revisions - December 5th 2026 Pilot training (optional time permitting) - December 2026 Final training package - December 2026 7. Climate and Environmental Impact The consultant should ensure that: The training promotes environmentally responsible vector control approaches. Environmental and ecological risks of vector control interventions are adequately addressed. Preference is given to sustainable and integrated vector management approaches. Training delivery methods minimize environmental impact where feasible. 8. Responsibilities and Communication The assignment will be coordinated by: Jan Heeger, WASH Programme Advisor, NLRC Selam Seje, Health Advisor, NLRC Joey de Hamer, Programme Manager, NLRC Peter Mamburi IFRC technical focal points Submission Deadline The proposal shall be submitted before the deadline for reception of applications on the 4th of October 2026. title: Finance Officer
description:
TITLE: Finance Officer JOB CATEGORY: Exempt (Salary) STATUS: Full-Time TYPE OF EMPLOYMENT: Regular Staff SUPERVISOR: Salama Hub Director REGION/UNIT: Africa Region LOCATION: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia GENERAL SUMMARY OF POSITION The finance officer will support the Salama Hub work by developing and upholding quality standards for financial control and management, building the capacity of staff and partners on financial implementation, accounting, and financial monitoring and evaluation of budgets for the program. The Finance Officer will be directly supervised by the Salama Hub Director and will work closely with the Regional Finance Manager for Africa. They will also collaborate with the IP Finance staff based in the central office in Philadelphia, the AFSC International Programs Finance Director, and other finance officers from collaborating agencies and partners to ensure a high degree of accountability and stewardship in the use of AFSC’s financial resources. The finance officer will directly supervise the Finance Assistant. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS / RESPONSIBILITIES Administer and review Salama Hub financial plans and budgets, monitor progress and changes, and keep the Salama Hub Director updated on the program’s financial status. Lead the annual budgeting and planning process in conjunction with BftW Consortium members, administer and review all financial plans and budgets, monitor progress and changes; and keep Consortium team members abreast of the Salama Hub’s financial status. Manage the monthly reconciliation of accounts payable and ensure that payment periods are adhered to and Salama Hub is in good standing and does not hold large amounts of unpaid liabilities. Manage the accounting and review all financial transactions and reporting related to the Salama Hub programs. Analyze and present financial reports in an accurate and timely manner. Effectively communicate and present critical financial matters to the Hub Director and the Regional Finance Manager. Ensure that all receivables are tracked, invoiced, paid, and correctly accounted for in a timely manner (including donor or partner receivables) Prepare the monthly and annual financial statements; collate financial reporting materials for all donor segments. Manage the monthly closing process for Account Payables and General Ledger for Salama Hub’s accounts. Process the Salama Hub Program payroll ensuring compliance with all statutory payments Ensure accurate implementation of all the Ethiopia Office finance policies and accounting practices, and ensure compliance and adherence to the policies Manage the Salama Hub’s cash flow and forecasting through proper monitoring of office liquidity position to ensure adequate funds are available for smooth office operations. Lead the program audit process by liaising with external auditors as well as being the main point of contact for donor (Bread for the World) program audits, including planning, scheduling, managing timeline, and deliverables in close collaboration with the Regional Finance Manager Ensure that staff are aware of the AFSC rules and procedures for budget and accounting using the AFSC regional finance manual, and AFSC finance directives as a guide. Undertake field visits from time to time to support partner finance staff and to carry out informal management and accounting audits as requested. Develop and maintain strong working relationships with external parties, including partner finance staff and banks. Perform any other duty as assigned by the supervisor from time to time. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS A bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or a related field with a minimum of 5 years of professional experience with an international organization, preferably an NGO, and should demonstrate an understanding of non-profit fund accounting practices. S/he must have ACCA or its equivalent. S/he must be fluent in spoken and written English. Expertise with MS Office applications (Word, Excel, Access, Outlook, PowerPoint); accounting software, payroll management systems & web-based communications platforms. Advanced Excel skills are highly preferred. Experience working with and implementing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. Wiliness and ability to travel across the Horn of Africa, sometimes on short notice, to project locations and partner sites. Ability to work effectively independently and within a team environment. Must be capable of working under tight time constraints in a high-volume environment with multiple priorities. Understanding of and commitment to the principles, concerns, and considerations, of AFSC in regard to issues of race, class, nationality, religion, age, gender and sexual orientation, and disabilities. Demonstrated ability to work and communicate with diverse staff. Commitment to Quaker values and testimonies. Understanding of and compatibility with the principles and philosophy of the American Friends Service Committee including non-violence and the belief in the intrinsic worth of every individual. PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands and work environment characteristics described are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. COMPENSATION The AFSC offers a competitive Total Rewards package which includes comprehensive medical and hospitalization insurance; term life, Short Term Disability & Long-Term Disability, defined benefit pension plan, plus other benefits including generous annual leave allocation, sabbaticals, extended leaves, and holidays. The American Friends Service Committee provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sec, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. The policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. AFSC’s Central Office and some of its offices in the U.S. are unionized workplaces. This position is not represented. AFSC maintains a deep commitment to a mandate of care for our staff and communities. The American Friends Service Committee is a smoke-free workplace.

How to Apply: Qualified candidates are encouraged to submit their applications, including a cover letter and an updated Curriculum Vitae( CV) as a single file with the subject line as “**Finance Officer- Salama Hub**” by email to: InfoAfrica@afsc.org on or before **6th November 2026.** Applicants should have a right to work in Ethiopia. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: HEAD OF OFFICE (M/F/D), ETHIOPIA
description:
The German Red Cross (GRC) assists people affected by disasters, crises and armed conflicts, and is a committed advocate for the fundamental principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Our Mission: We provide needs-based, flexible, innovative and sustainable support to Sister National Societies, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the wider humanitarian community. We enable early and immediate life-saving assistance and implement anticipatory action and risk-reducing activities, particularly in the face of climate change and armed conflicts and their humanitarian consequences. As a partner, facilitator and convener of cooperation, we strive to fulfil commitments to localization, community participation, protection and inclusion, gender and diversity, accountability, and learning. Through these efforts, we aim to build resilient communities and ensure effective and inclusive humanitarian responses in an increasingly complex global landscape. The GRC is currently seeking an experienced Head of Office (m/f/d) to lead its Country Office in Ethiopia. The GRC has a long-standing partnership with the Ethiopian Red Crescent Society (ERCS). At present, the primary focus of GRC lies in providing assistance to the ERCS in addressing the ongoing crisis and humanitarian needs and adjusting the existing portfolio according to the changing needs and according to ERCS priorities The GRC is committed to support its Sister Society where possible and work with the ERCS team to jointly decide on long-term programmes which fall within ERCS strategic priorities through joint programs, exchange of knowledge as well as technical and managerial support. The Head of Office (HoO) is located in Addis Abeba. He/she directly supervises the international GRC delegates and national staff and is responsible for the overall security management. The HoO reports to the country manager at GRC HQ in Berlin. Starting date: 01.01.2027 Duration: 12 months (with possible extension) Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with frequent visits to the project sites Main duties & responsibilities: Strategic leadership and representation: Lead the GRC Country Office and represent the GRC in Ethiopia vis-à-vis ERCS, the wider Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, government authorities, the German Embassy, donors, national and international humanitarian organisations and other relevant stakeholders. Maintain strong partnerships and networks and contribute to the positioning and visibility of the GRC in the country. Support ERCS in building and strengthening their capacities and programmes in line with the ERCS National Society Development (NSD) strategy. Partnership and Movement coordination: Ensure close coordination and cooperation with ERCS and support the implementation of the IFRC Ways of Working (WoW) localisation initiatives and other efforts to strengthen ERCS capacities. Represent the GRC in relevant Movement coordination platforms, including the MOC, CCT and technical working groups (TWGs), and foster synergies with Movement partners. Country strategy and programme development: Further develop and adapt the GRC country strategy and operational portfolio in line with the evolving humanitarian context, needs assessments and ERCS priorities. Identify funding opportunities and lead or contribute to the development of concept notes and project proposals in coordination with ERCS, GRC Headquarters and Movement partners. Financial and administrative management of the country office: Oversee the financial and administrative management of the Country Office, including budgeting, expenditure monitoring, procurement, human resources, inventories and the management of fixed and financial assets. Ensure that appropriate systems, structures and procedures are in place and implemented in accordance with GRC guidelines and applicable donor regulations, in close coordination with the finance and project delegates. Direct line-management of GRC delegates and support of staff development and capacity building of national and international team. Programme and project management: Oversee the implementation of GRC-supported programmes and ensure high-quality, timely and effective delivery in line with approved objectives, budgets and work plans. Monitor programme progress, assess results and risks, and ensure compliance with GRC policies and donor requirements, including those of BMZ, GFFO and ECHO. Ensure timely and accurate narrative and financial reporting. Where required, directly manage emergency response projects in close coordination with ERCS Headquarters, local ERCS branches, project teams and volunteers. Context monitoring and analysis: Monitor and analyse relevant political, socio-economic, humanitarian and security developments, with a particular focus on humanitarian needs, disaster risks and their implications for GRC operations. effective information sharing with GRC Headquarters and external stakeholders. Security management: Ensure that security policies, procedures and contingency plans are regularly reviewed, updated and followed by all staff. Coordinate security management with relevant Movement partners, and ensure compliance with applicable security arrangements, including the L2 agreement with the ICRC. Leadership and capacity strengthening: Directly supervise and support international delegates and national staff, promoting professional development, team cohesion and a positive working environment. Support ERCS in strengthening its organisational capacities and programmes in line with its National Society Development (NSD) strategy. Ensure communication, visibility and information sharing on GRC/ERCS programmes with all stakeholders, including project beneficiaries, partners, local authorities and donors. Required Competencies & Skills: Technical experience: University degree in a relevant field. At least five years of professional experience in international cooperation, including substantial experience in humanitarian crisis and/or development contexts. Demonstrated experience in programme and project management, including budgeting, financial monitoring, programme quality assurance, monitoring and evaluation, and donor reporting. Experience in staff management, team leadership and capacity strengthening. Previous experience leading a country office for a humanitarian organisation, managing international teams and overseeing security management is an asset. Technical expertise in one or more of the following areas: WASH, shelter and non-food items (NFI), anticipatory action, cash and voucher assistance, health/pre-hospital emergency care (PHEC), food security or livelihoods. Sound understanding of the humanitarian system, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and disaster management. Experience within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement is a strong asset. Substantial experience implementing donor-funded projects. Familiarity with BMZ, GFFO and ECHO funding requirements is a strong asset. Proven experience in organisational development, capacity building and team coaching. Experience working in the Greater Horn of Africa, particularly Ethiopia, is an asset. Personal skills: Excellent leadership, diplomatic, communication, negotiation and networking skills, with the ability to represent the organisation effectively and engage with diverse stakeholders. Strategic thinking combined with a hands-on, pragmatic and solution-oriented approach. Strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to prioritise and make decisions in complex and rapidly changing environments. Excellent intercultural sensitivity and the ability to work independently while fostering effective teamwork. Resilience and strong stress-management skills, including the ability to work in insecure and conflict-affected environments. Knowledge of policies and procedures relating to safety and security, Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), compliance and human resources development. Fluency in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Amharic and/or German is an advantage. Excellent computer skills, including spreadsheets, word-processing software, databases and other relevant applications. Readiness to travel to and work in remote areas is essential. Experience of living and working in insecure and conflict-affected environments is an asset. Ability to work independently and as a team member; Ability and agreement to adhere to the Red Cross Red Crescent Fundamental Principles; Ability to complete a thorough medical screening process 'working abroad under specific climate and health conditions’; Valid International Driving Permit (IDP). What we offer you: You will be part of a highly motivated professional and multicultural team. We offer you a compensation package according to the collective employment agreement of the GRC, an expatriation allowance during your mission. In addition to a full insurance package GRC is covering a home flight within a 12-months period of assignment. You will benefit from a comprehensive training package and receive briefings and coaching prior as well as during and after your mission. Medical check-ups and Psychosocial Support Service are included in your assignment.

How to Apply: **Kindly apply by submitting your application by using the** [**GRC online application**](https://karriere-beim-drk.de/mv36a) **system until 15.11.2026.** Please note that due to the travel and visa regulations and the guidelines of our partners in the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement certain vaccinations are required for this delegate position. Candidates on the short-list for this position will be asked to disclose their vaccination status. [HEAD OF OFFICE (M/F/D), ETHIOPIA](https://karriere-beim-drk.de/onm87) We point out that the selection and nomination processes for this international delegate position may demand that information concerning your person be shared with involved Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners (IFRC, ICRC, National Society). This may include transmission into countries that do not apply data protection standards comparable to those of the European Union.

title: Regional Safety & Security Director
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Context The East Africa region supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges – conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation – through integrated, impactful approaches. The region prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration. The region responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. EA focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs. The EA region operates country programs in Uganda, Kenya, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, and Ethiopia. Position Summary The Regional Safety and Security Director (RSSD) is one of the most senior leadership roles in the East Africa region and provides strategic leadership for safety, security, and humanitarian access across the region. They set and drive the implementation of a comprehensive strategy to anticipate, analyze, and mitigate risks, safeguard staff and assets, enable principled humanitarian access, and ensure the continuity of IRC’s operations and programs in complex and high-risk environments. As the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the Regional Vice President (RVP), the RSSD works alongside the RVP on the decisions that shape IRC’s presence, access, and continuity across the region. They are a full member of the Regional Management Team and of IRC’s global safety and security (S&S) team. Within the Regional Management Team, the RSSD contributes as a senior leader to regional strategy, priorities, and decision-making, not only as the safety and security function, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices. They integrate Gender, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (GEDI) informed security risk analysis into strategic, operational, programmatic, and partnership decisions so that security considerations are embedded across IRC’s work. Reporting jointly to the RVP and the Senior Director for Safety and Security (SDSS), the RSSD operates with significant autonomy and influence. Working in close partnership with Country Directors, they ensure that each country program has robust, context-appropriate protocols, systems, and capacities in place to address unique threats and challenges, while remaining agile to adapt to shifting environments. The RSSD maintains in-depth knowledge of security dynamics across all EA countries, monitors early warning indicators, and deploys regularly, including at short notice, to support local teams. They play a central role in mentoring and building the capabilities of IRC staff and leaders to operate safely and effectively, thereby strengthening IRC’s ability to reach and serve the most affected and underserved populations. Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Regional Management As a member of the Regional Management Team, contribute as a senior leader to regional strategy, priority-setting, and decision-making, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices across the region rather than representing the safety and security function alone. Serve as the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the RVP, enabling timely, risk-informed decisions on humanitarian access, operational continuity, and duty of care, and jointly activating and leading crisis management when required. Partner with Country Directors to align safety, security, and humanitarian access with country Strategy Action Plans (SAPs) and operational priorities, supporting their decision-making and accountability for risk. Security Risk Management Lead and supervise the identification, analysis, and mitigation of S&S risks across the region, ensuring alignment with IRC’s global standards. Guide and support Country Directors and field leaders to adapt and implement context-specific security risk management strategies ensuring proactive risk identification, mitigation, and emergency preparedness. Review, monitor, and encourage compliance with the Security Minimum Standards (SMS) in all country programs providing follow-up and technical guidance where gaps are identified. Drive and champion the development, adaptation, and roll-out of global and regional initiatives on duty of care and safeguarding, embedding these into operational culture and practice. Shape and strengthen safety and security policies, procedures, and practices that fully integrate Gender Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (GEDI) principles as well as Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) commitments. Extend IRC’s security capacity to partners, ensuring they receive tailored risk management support, access to systems, and benefit from IRC’s standards relevant to their operational contexts. Build and maintain an active network of IRC security focal points across country programs and cultivate strong external relationships with professional contacts, peer agencies, and security counterparts to enhance collective risk management. Humanitarian Access Management Enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access across country programs, ensuring communities can be reached and served in line with IRC’s country Strategy Action Plans (SAP). Strengthen and expand humanitarian access teams and capabilities across the region, building skills, systems, and approaches that enhance operational reach and acceptance. Develop, adapt, and implement context-specific guidelines for humanitarian access and engagement with state and non-state actors, ensuring alignment with IRC policy, international humanitarian law, and standards. Advise and guide country programs in the design of operational and programmatic contingency plans ensuring preparedness for sudden shifts in political, security, or conflict dynamics. Collaborate with relevant IRC units to ensure prompt and appropriate follow-up to violations of IRC’s Code of Conduct and breaches of humanitarian principles, reinforcing accountability and ethical operations. Performance Management and Development Lead and actively contribute to the recruitment and selection of key positions with S&S responsibilities, ensuring high-caliber talent and diverse representation. Co-manage and mentor direct-report staff (under the Management in Partnership (MiP) model with Country Directors), setting clear expectations, defining performance objectives, providing regular, timely feedback, and conducting documented performance reviews that drive accountability and growth. Promote and safeguard staff well-being, monitoring staff care across the region and supporting appropriate interventions to address the needs of both national and international staff. Directly supervise and develop the Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Coordinator, ensuring progressive and forward-looking S&S plans that align with regional priorities and organizational strategy. Learning & Development Design, support, and supervise the implementation of regional capacity-building plans, ensuring effective delivery of IRC’s global S&S training programs across EA country programs. Embed gender-sensitive approaches into all capacity development and learning initiatives, addressing gender-specific risks and ensuring inclusivity in staff preparedness. Lead and facilitate critical incident management trainings and simulations, in close coordination with the global S&S unit to strengthen preparedness and response capacities across the region. Incident Management Support country programs to ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality incident notification, reporting, analysis, and dissemination of lessons learned. Serve as a member of the Regional Incident Management Team actively supporting the RVP in the management and resolution of Tier 2 and Tier 3 incidents. Facilitate After-Action Reviews ensuring that corrective measures are clearly defined, documented, and systematically implemented in line with established incident protocols. Oversee and monitor the SHIELD incident database producing quarterly trend analyses to inform strategic decision-making and strengthen regional risk mitigation. title: Pre-Hospital Emergency Care (PHEC) Delegate Ethiopia (m/f/d)
description:
The German Red Cross (GRC) assists people affected by disasters, crises and armed conflicts, and is a committed advocate for the fundamental principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Our Mission: We provide needs-based, flexible, innovative and sustainable support to Sister National Societies, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the wider humanitarian community. We enable early and immediate life-saving assistance and implement anticipatory action and risk-reducing activities, particularly in the face of climate change and armed conflicts and their humanitarian consequences. As a partner, facilitator and convener of cooperation, we strive to fulfil commitments to localization, community participation, protection and inclusion, gender and diversity, accountability, and learning. Through these efforts, we aim to build resilient communities and ensure effective and inclusive humanitarian responses in an increasingly complex global landscape. The GRC is currently seeking a Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC) Delegate Ethiopia (m/f/d) . The Delegate will advise the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) and the GRC on prehospital emergency care (PHEC) and related health matters. In addition, the Delegate will oversee the implementation of a new project funded under the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)’s Social Structure Funding (SSF) programme, in close cooperation with ERCS. The three-year project, entitled “Strengthening the Ethiopian Red Cross Society as a key actor in the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) system and improving the national enabling environment,” is planned to run from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2029. It aims to strengthen ERCS’s institutional and technical capacities in Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and contribute to the further development and standardisation of EMS in Ethiopia. Key areas include capacity building, the development and implementation of national guidelines and policies, and strengthening coordination and quality assurance within the national EMS system. The Delegate will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia and work under the supervision of the Head of Office and will be part of an experienced team of three international delegates and local staff. The position is subject to final confirmation of BMZ funding. Starting date: 01.01.2027 Duration: 24 months, with possible extension Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with frequent visits to the project sites Main duties & responsibilities Provide technical advice and contribute to strengthening ERCS capacities in Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC), Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and related health areas , including through the development and implementation of national standards, guidelines, training approaches and quality assurance mechanisms, capacity building and training-of-trainers approaches, and support to the institutionalisation and sustainability of PHEC and EMS services. Oversee the implementation of the BMZ SSF-funded EMS project in close cooperation with the ERCS, including project planning, reporting and budget management, ensuring effective, timely and quality implementation in line with the approved project proposal, budget and donor requirements. Ensure close coordination with relevant national and international stakeholders , including the Ethiopian Ministry of Health, NGOs, Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners providing technical support to health-related activities, and other actors working in health, particularly in PHEC. Represent GRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups and related clusters. Support project monitoring, learning and quality assurance , including regular monitoring of activities and results, collection and analysis of project data and indicators, identification of implementation challenges, and follow-up on agreed actions. Support the identification and development of opportunities for additional funding for PHEC activities from other institutional and private funding sources. Provide support in emergencies in the area of PHEC and beyond , as requested by ERCS and GRC. Required Competencies & Skills University degree in Paramedicine/Prehospital Emergency Care, Public/Global Health, Health Management, Disaster Management or a related field. A clinical background as a paramedic, emergency nurse or physician with prehospital experience is an asset. At least five years of professional experience in Prehospital Emergency Care (PHEC), emergency care, humanitarian health or a related field. Strong technical knowledge and practical experience in PHEC , ideally including experience in the development or implementation of PHEC systems, standards, guidelines, training programmes, quality assurance mechanisms and/or referral systems. Demonstrated project management experience , including project planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, budget management and financial monitoring of donor-funded projects. Experience with BMZ-funded projects is an asset. Experience in capacity strengthening and adult learning , including the design and facilitation of trainings, workshops and/or training-of-trainers approaches. Previous experience working with the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and knowledge of its structures, approaches and Fundamental Principles are strong assets. Experience in multi-stakeholder coordination , preferably with government authorities, National Societies, international organisations and other health or PHEC actors. Strong communication, coordination and representation skills , with the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with partners at different organisational levels. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and effectively in complex and changing environments , with a high degree of cultural sensitivity and adaptability. Excellent written and spoken English . Knowledge of German is an asset. Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a multicultural and multidisciplinary team . title: Request for Proposals: Financial and Risk Management Compliance Audits for Sub-Grantees
description:
Request for Proposals: Financial and Risk Management Compliance Audits for Sub-Grantees Background and context Tiko engages various partners, including Community-Based Organizations (CBOs), Quality Assurance providers, SGBV service providers, and safe houses, through formal Sub-Grant Agreements to deliver community and health response services. These partnerships are critical for reaching adolescents and young women (AGYW). To ensure programmatic integrity, financial stewardship, robust risk management, and the highest standards of financial governance, Tiko requires periodic and comprehensive financial and risk management compliance audits of these entities. The relevant locations for this scope are: Kenya: Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Machakos, Nakuru, Migori, Kilifi, Homa Bay, Bungoma, Nyamira, Kisii, Busia and Kakamega counties. Uganda: Wakiso and Kampala districts. Ethiopia: Addis Ababa and Hawassa. South Africa: City of Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane. Nigeria: Abuja FCT and Nasarawa. Burkina Faso: Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso. Firms can apply for one or more markets where they can demonstrate the ability to deliver the assignments. Firms must be registered in each country where they seek to provide the services. Objective of the audit The primary objective is to verify that sub-grantees are operating in full compliance with the financial, risk management, and statutory requirements of their signed grant agreements and relevant regulatory standards. The audit will assess: Financial accountability, internal controls, and complete expenditure documentation. Compliance with anti-fraud, anti-corruption, and financial risk governance mandates. Accuracy, integrity, and reconciliation of financial and transactional data across reporting frameworks. Adherence to statutory obligations, procurement guidelines, and budget line allocations. Scope of audit Expenditure verification: Reconcile transaction listings, general ledgers, and bank statements against approved budget lines and the project scope of work. Milestone achievement: Verify that disbursements are linked to confirmed deliverables as per the signed agreements. Expenditure verification and anti-double dipping: Verify that all incurred expenditures are legitimate, supported by adequate documentation, and that there is no “double dipping” or duplicate funding from other sources for the same activities. External audit review: Review external audit management reports and prior audit findings for the last two financial years. Test to ensure that all recommendations arising from findings have been implemented. Procurement compliance: Inspect procurement documentation to ensure competitive bidding policies were followed. Internal controls: Evaluate sub-recipient internal controls, including segregation of duties, delegation of authority, and financial software controls. Conduct walkthroughs for various cycles, including payments, payroll and assets, ensuring they are in line with policy. Statutory compliance: Confirm compliance with statutory obligations, including tax filings, labour laws, and anti-corruption policies. Deliverables Audit plan: Detailed timeline and 100% review for selected sub-grantees. Individual audit reports: Comprehensive audit reports for each sub-grantee featuring granular findings, objective risk ratings (Compliant / Partially Compliant / Non-Compliant), root-cause analysis of compliance gaps, and actionable, time-bound Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) complete with clear implementation deadlines, designated responsible owners, and re-verification milestones to ensure full risk mitigation. Summary consolidation: High-level overview of systemic compliance gaps and recommended training/capacity-building interventions. Qualifications of firms and proposed personnel The selected firm and its proposed personnel must demonstrate a comprehensive profile aligned with financial audit and risk compliance requirements. Mandatory qualifications include: Extensive experience in conducting financial, forensic, and risk compliance audits within the NGO and development sectors. Proven technical expertise in financial risk management, internal controls assessment, and fraud prevention/detection methodologies. Certified financial and risk audit professionals, such as CPA, ACCA, CFE, or equivalent certifications. Strong analytical skills in financial data reconciliation, transaction testing, and identifying systemic governance and control gaps. Experience in reviewing grant agreements, evaluating statutory compliance, and producing actionable financial audit reports. Evaluation criteria Proposals should: Be clear about the relevant skills, experience and capacity of the participant in respect of this particular scope of work. Contain details of the proposed approach to be adopted to deliver the service in accordance with the scope of work. Clearly indicate whether bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work. Clearly indicate compliance with the appropriate data protection, privacy, legal, social, tax and ethical requirements applicable to each country applied for. Bidders must be registered firms in the countries where they seek to provide the services. A firm can bid for one or more markets depending on capacity. Proposals will be evaluated against the following criteria: 1. Experience, skills and ability of the service provider — 30% Past experience in similar work of this nature. Team member experience, accompanied by brief CVs. Ability of the bidder to fulfil Tiko’s requirements. 2. Technical approach and execution plan — 30% Proposals must contain details of the proposed approach to be adopted to deliver the service in accordance with the scope of work. 3. Financial quotation — 10% Proposals should clearly indicate whether bid participants have the financial capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work, based on the previous value of similar work undertaken, for example by sharing copies of recent audited financial statements. 4. References — 10% Submission of at least three relevant and contactable clients previously served. 5. Capacity — 20% Proposals should clearly indicate whether bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work. Total: 100%

How to Apply: **Proposal submission guidelines** Registered firms are invited to submit proposals for this engagement. Firms may apply for one or more markets and must clearly identify the countries covered by their proposals. Proposals should include the contents below and must not exceed 15 pages, excluding annexures comprising the budget and summary profiles of proposed personnel: 1. **Cover page:** Summary with basic information such as the firm’s name, address, contact information, proposed budget and countries applied for. 2. **Capacity statement:** A brief capacity statement explaining why your firm and proposed team are well positioned to undertake the engagement. 3. **Qualifications to the scope of work:** Any qualifications or reservations that you may have regarding the scope of work. 4. **Proposed approach:** Your proposed approach to delivering the scope of work requirements. 5. **Proposed personnel:** The qualifications and experience of the proposed personnel. 6. **Work plan:** Proposed work plan with tasks, responsible persons and timeline. 7. **Financial proposal:** Hourly rates in USD for each proposed role/position identified in the proposal. 8. **References:** At least three relevant and contactable references for similar engagements undertaken by the firm in the last five years. The submission must be clear, concise, and complete. Applicants should submit only such information as is necessary to respond effectively to this request for proposals. Unless specifically requested, extraneous presentation materials are neither necessary nor desired. **Expression of interest and clarification questions** Interested firms are requested to express their interest and/or submit clarification questions by emailing **bidding@tiko.org** on or before **Thursday, 22 October 2026 at 12h00 South African Standard Time (SAST, UTC+2)**. Use the subject line: **Sub-Grantee Compliance Audits: \[Firm name\]** Tiko will circulate consolidated clarification responses to all firms that have registered their interest by **Monday, 26 October 2026 at 12h00 SAST,** whether or not they submitted questions. **Submission deadline** Submit technical and financial proposals by email to [**bidding@tiko.org**](https://reliefweb.int/bidding@tiko.org) no later than **Friday, 30 October 2026 at 12h00 midday South African Standard Time (SAST, UTC+2 / 10h00 UTC)**. Use the subject line: **RFP – Sub-Grantee Compliance Audits – \[Country/Countries\]: \[Firm name\]**

title: Global Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) Manager

title: Head of Advocacy and Evidencing
description:
Location: Ethiopia, India, Italy, Jordan, Kenya (as long as HelpAge International holds the registration in this country), Nepal, Pakistan, Spain, Tanzania, Thailand, Türkiye, United Kingdom and Zimbabwe Department: Global Impact Reports to (Line Manager): Director of Global Impact Responsible for (Line managing) Humanitarian Advocacy Advisor Social Protection Advisor Health Advisor Rights Advisor Grade: F Contract Type: Open-ended contract About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. About the Job The Head of Advocacy & Evidencing provides strategic leadership and organisational accountability for HelpAge’s global advocacy, policy and research agendas, ensuring that external engagement is grounded in rigorous evidence, shaped by the lived experiences of older people, and aligned with organisational priorities. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities To deliver impact, the Head of Advocacy & Evidencing will: Lead the delivery and evolution of HelpAge’s global advocacy and research agenda, ensuring it reflects lived experience and drives progress on rights, inclusion, and equity for older people. Strengthen the capacities of network members and older people to lead and participate meaningfully in advocacy efforts, and ensure inclusive engagement in the design and implementation of influencing strategies. Cultivate strategic partnerships with policy, academic, and research institutions to co-produce high-quality, policy-relevant evidence and promote HelpAge’s thought leadership on rights, healthy ageing, humanitarian inclusion, and social protection. Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Advocacy Lead and be accountable for the development, implementation and results of HelpAge’s global advocacy and evidencing strategy, aligned with HelpAge’s impact areas and co-created with network members. Monitor and respond to global, regional and national policy trends,advising colleagues and network members on opportunities for engagement and influence. Champion inclusive, partner-led advocacy approaches that centre the voices and leadership of older people and civil society actors. Collaborate with the Fundraising and Strategic Partnerships Director and supporting members to align donor advocacy efforts with organisational priorities and global influencing strategies. Advise the Executive Leadership Group and the Board on HelpAge's advocacy positions and external positioning, and lead the preparation and quality of the related papers and briefings. Where appropriate, represent HelpAge's positions externally alongside senior leaders. Lead and coordinate HelpAge's influencing in priority global and regional policy and donor markets, including Europe, identifying opportunities to position ageing and the rights of older people within relevant policy, development and humanitarian agendas and, in collaboration with Fundraising, strengthen HelpAge's positioning with institutional donors and partners. Be accountable for achieving the agreed Advocacy & Evidencing income target. Working in partnership with the Fundraising & Strategic Partnerships team, play a lead technical and relationship role in shaping fundable propositions, contributing to pipeline development, and donor cultivation and stewardship for advocacy and research. Ensure that advocacy, research and evidence-generation activities comply with HelpAge’s ethical, safeguarding, data protection and relevant organisational standards, and hold team members accountable for compliance within their areas of responsibility. Represent HelpAge at senior level in key global and regional coalitions, alliances and policy forums, proactively building strategic relationships with governments, multilateral and donor institutions, policy actors and other influential stakeholders to advance HelpAge’s advocacy priorities and strengthen its external positioning. Evidence and Research Lead and be accountable for HelpAge’s global research and evidence agenda, ensuring that it is coherent, ethical, inclusive and aligned with organisational advocacy and programme priorities. Provide strategic oversight of HelpAge’s global portfolio of evidence generation, policy analysis and advocacy initiatives across key impact areas, ensuring coherence, quality and alignment with organisational strategy and drawing on the network as a central source of evidence and insight. Foster partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks, and research bodies to co-produce and validate robust, policy-influencing evidence. Ensure that research outputs are accessible, actionable, and designed for strategic influence at global and national levels. Capacity Strengthening and Network Engagement Lead on advocacy capacity strengthening of HelpAge network members and older people through mentoring, training, and tailored support. Promote knowledge exchange and peer learning across the global network, ensuring inclusive participation in advocacy platforms and decision-making spaces. Collaborate with regional colleagues to support the development and implementation of national and regional advocacy strategies led by network members. Team and Resource Management Lead, manage, and coach a multidisciplinary team of advocacy advisers, ensuring high performance and alignment with organisational goals. These are hybrid roles, with approximately 50% of their time dedicated to global advocacy and the remaining 50% focused on technical support to network members and contribution to programme development. Manage advocacy and research budgets effectively, ensuring compliance with donor requirements and strategic resource allocation. Cross-Organisational Collaboration Work closely with Programme Support, Network Development, MEAL, Fundraising, and Communications teams to embed evidence and influencing in all areas of work. Coordinate joint advocacy and research initiatives that connect policy engagement with programme delivery and impact measurement. Skills and experience required Essential Proven strategic leadership in global advocacy, policy influencing, and research within the international development, humanitarian, or human rights sectors. Strong leadership, planning, and performance management skills, with a track record of delivering results through high-performing, diverse, and remote multidisciplinary teams. Deep understanding and practical application of rights-based, inclusive, and intersectional approaches—especially relating to age, gender, disability, and displacement. Demonstrated success in designing and implementing partner-led advocacy strategies that centre lived experience and community priorities. Experience influencing policy at national, regional and international levels through coalition-building and senior-level relationships with governments, multilateral bodies and donors. Strong analytical and research skills, with experience designing or overseeing ethical, participatory research and translating evidence into compelling policy and advocacy outputs. Demonstrated ability to build and sustain high-impact partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks and policy platforms. Track record of securing income for advocacy or research, including developing fundable propositions and engaging institutional donors with fundraising colleagues. Skilled in budget oversight and resource management, including accountability in donor-funded initiatives. Ability to monitor advocacy impact, policy trends, and funding landscapes, and to adapt strategies accordingly. Experience of strengthening the capacity of civil society, networks or grassroots movements, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, through mentoring, training and tailored support. Lived experience of the Global South or extensive professional experience working in Global South contexts. Desirable Strong knowledge and networks in European/global institutional policy and donor environments Experience engaging with media to support advocacy. Education and Qualifications Degree in international development, public policy, human rights, social sciences, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience). A postgraduate qualification is an asset but not essential where practical experience is strong. Other Requirements Willingness to travel internationally Ability to work across cultures, sectors, and geographies in inclusive and equitable ways. Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable. Deep commitment to locally led development and the principles of Partner-Led Programming. We actively value and encourage candidates with lived experience of inequality, marginalisation, or systemic exclusion—especially related to age, gender, disability, displacement, or economic injustice. Familiarity with ageing, inclusion, and rights issues in Global South contexts is a key asset. Key Behavioural Competencies Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organisations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together. Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further. Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged. Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners. Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination. Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Safeguarding HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for: Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work. Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism. Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices. Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures. SAFER RECRUITMENT All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
description:
Desired start date: 01/12/2026 Duration of the mission: 6 Months Location: Adwa - Tigray Region SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms. PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION: Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region). In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors. In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement. SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area. GENERAL OBJECTIVES : The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone. Representation and Internal / external communication: The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep). ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES : Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements. PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS : -Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams. -Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans. -Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components. -Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring. -Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies. -Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context -Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities SECURITY CONSTRAINTS : The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making. YOUR PROFIL : DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required. EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years TECHNICAL SKILLS : Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes. TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection). LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset. SI WILL OFFER YOU : A salaried position: According to experience, starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400. SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment. Breaks: During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked. Insurance package: Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded. Living conditions: Guest House conditions : - There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit. -Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa -Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa : - Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

title: Physiotherapist
description:
The Physiotherapist is responsible for the treatment, counselling, preventative care and rehabilitation of the motor function and physical wellness of the patients. is responsible for assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating individualized rehabilitation programs for patients with limb loss and other mobility impairments. Working within a multidisciplinary team, the Physiotherapist facilitates functional recovery, promotes independence, optimizes prosthetic use, and improves patients’ quality of life through evidence-based rehabilitation practices The Physiotherapist tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following points: Undertake a comprehensive and accurate assessment of patients in a variety of settings; Identify, plan and manage physiotherapy interventions and rehabilitation plans Provide physio treatments to achieve identified outcomes and monitor patients’ conditions, both for in-patients and out-patients, if needed; Perform all the tasks related to the physio competence framework; Establish, maintain and conclude therapeutic interpersonal relationships with patients and their relatives, based on respect, dignity and care; Conduct comprehensive physical assessments of patients with upper and lower limb amputations, including musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, balance, gait, and functional evaluations. Provide pre-prosthetic rehabilitation, including: residual limb care and shaping, edema management, scar management, pain management (including phantom limb pain where appropriate), range of motion and strengthening exercises, contracture prevention Cardiovascular conditioning Deliver prosthetic rehabilitation, including: prosthetic gait training, balance and coordination training, functional mobility training Stair negotiation and community ambulation Transfers and activities of daily living (ADL) training Fall prevention strategies Monitor patient progress and modify treatment plans according to clinical outcomes. Encourage patients to have a positive attitude towards physiotherapy by motivating them; Organizing daily group activities, if possible, for patients; Promote an environment that enables patient’s safety and health implementing all necessary actions such as infection control practices, bed sores prevention practices and maintaining high level of hygiene also ensuring physio material are properly cleaned; Ensure that the equipment is functional and well maintained and stored; Ensure documentation/record is accurate and physio chart is properly filled, maintaining confidentially of information; Compiling and submitting periodic reports, if requested, following EMERGENCY guidelines; Be compliant with EMERGENCY guidelines for the treatment of patients; Work closely with prosthetists/orthotists during prosthetic prescription, fitting, alignment, and follow-up. Provide clinical feedback regarding prosthetic fit, function, comfort, and patient performance. Participate in training programs or activities, meeting timelines and deliverables, if requested by EMERGENCY; Train new staff, if needed. Job requirements: Degree in the Physio field; (Bachelor’s Degree in Physiotherapy from a recognized institution). Postgraduate training in rehabilitation, prosthetics, amputee rehabilitation, or neurorehabilitation Experience working in prosthetic and orthotic services. Good problem solving, time management and technical skills and willingness to learn new procedures and techniques; Good communication, interpersonal skills and high level of empathy, patience and ability to handle emotional and pressure situations; Basic Computer Skills, including Microsoft Office Program; Good level of English, written and spoken.
